In this file the predictions of model 1 are computed on the test set . The predictions are computed for OLS, local shrinkage and ridge methods. The local shrinkage and ridge regression methods are fitted using the optimal parameter estimated in file: "model 1- Cross Validation"

```{r}
#loading of libraries and data
library(Hmisc)
library(ggplot2)
library(MASS)
library(dplyr)
library(glmnet)
getHdata(gusto)
gusto.dat <- gusto

set.seed(4176340)
gusto.dat <- gusto[which(gusto$grpl %in% c(1,2,4) & gusto$grps %in% c(5,9,10,11)),]



```

Train and test set partition
```{r}
# build test and training sets.
# parameter : size        'training size'
size = 0.7

n.1 <- nrow(gusto.dat)
train_index <- sample(1:n.1, size = size * n.1)
train_set <- gusto.dat[train_index, ]
test_set  <- gusto.dat[-train_index, ]
n_pat <- nrow(train_set)  
train_set$pat.id <- 1:n_pat
train_set$HEI <- train_set$height
train_set$WEI <- train_set$weight
train_set$AGE <- train_set$age
train_set$SYS <- train_set$sysbp
train_set$PUL <- train_set$pulse

test_set$HEI <- test_set$height
test_set$WEI <- test_set$weight
test_set$AGE <- test_set$age
test_set$SYS <- test_set$sysbp
test_set$PUL <- test_set$pulse

```

Ordinary Least Squares - train set
```{r}
# linear OLS
# parameter: data      'train set'
#            form1     'response ~ predictors'

form1 <- WEI ~ HEI + AGE + PUL + SYS  #model 1
mod_OLS_base <- lm(formula = form1, data = train_set)
X_ols <- model.matrix(~HEI+AGE+PUL+SYS, data= train_set)  
X_ols_test <- model.matrix(~HEI+AGE+PUL+SYS, data= test_set) 



XTX <- t(X_ols)%*%X_ols
relvar_OLS <- numeric(length = nrow(X_ols))  #inverse of effective sample size for the train set is computed
for(i in 1:length(relvar_OLS)){
  relvar_OLS[i] <- (t(X_ols[i,])%*%solve(XTX)%*%X_ols[i,])
} 
```
Ordinary Least Squares - test set predictions
```{r}
pred_ols <- predict(mod_OLS_base, newdata = test_set) #predictions OLS on the test set
```


local shrinkage algorithm:

```{r}
## Initialization training shrinkage

Z_ols      <- X_ols[,-1] #predictors without intercept
n          <- nrow(Z_ols) 
Z_shrink   <- Z_ols    #copy of the covariates that will be shrank
relvar_it  <- relvar_OLS #copy of hii
z_bar      <- colMeans(Z_shrink)  #average per predictor value
zc         <- t(apply(X=Z_shrink, MARGIN = 1, FUN = function(x){x-z_bar})) #covariates are centered
X_shrink   <- cbind(icpt=rep(1,n), Z_shrink) #design matrix + intercept 
iter       <- 0 
maxiter    <- 1000
dist       <- n*relvar_it - 1  #distance
diststart  <- dist  

```

CV gives 50 as the best threshold for this model
```{r}
#THRESHOLD FOR SHRINKAGE.
# parameter:  neff_min          'effective sample size'

neff_min <- 50

max_dist <- n*1/neff_min -1  #threshold for shrinkage
```

Local shrinkage on the training set
```{r}
while(max(dist) > max_dist & iter < maxiter){ #while loop until all distances are below the threshold
  
  ## compute the shrinked distance
  distshrink  <- dist
  distshrink[which(dist>max_dist)] <- max_dist 
  
  # compute shrinkage factor
  a           <- sqrt(distshrink/dist)
  
  
  azc         <- a*zc #  #shrink of the centered covariates
  Z_shrink    <- t(apply(X=azc, MARGIN = 1, FUN = function(x){x + z_bar})) 
  
  iter <- iter + 1  
  ## step 1
  X_shrink   <- cbind(icpt=rep(1,n), Z_shrink)  #adding the intercept
  
  z_bar      <- colMeans(Z_shrink) 
  
  zc         <- t(apply(X=Z_shrink, MARGIN = 1, FUN = function(x){x-z_bar})) 
  
  
  Cov        <- ginv(t(X_shrink)%*%X_shrink) #XTX
  
  relvar_it  <- diag(X_shrink %*% Cov %*% t(X_shrink))  #the inverse of XTX 
  
  n_eff      <- 1/relvar_it 
  
  dist       <- n*relvar_it - 1  
}
```

Effective sample size computed on the test set
```{r}
#test set distances 
relvar_OLS_test <- numeric(length = nrow(X_ols_test))  
for(i in 1:length(relvar_OLS_test)){
  relvar_OLS_test[i] <- (t(X_ols_test[i,])%*%Cov%*%X_ols_test[i,])
}

n.test <- nrow(X_ols_test)
test_distance <- n*relvar_OLS_test-1 #test set distances

sum((1/relvar_OLS_test)<50) #only 3 test set subjects have an effective sample size smaller than the threshold 
```
Local shrinkage on the test set
```{r}
distshrink_test <- pmin(test_distance, max_dist) #distance shrinkage

a_test <-  sqrt(distshrink_test / test_distance) #tesy shrinkage factor

Z_ols_test   <- X_ols_test[,-1] 

Z_shrink_test <- Z_ols_test 

relvar_it_test <- relvar_OLS_test

zc_test        <- t(apply(X=Z_shrink_test, MARGIN = 1, FUN = function(x){x-z_bar})) 

azc_test <-zc_test*a_test #shrinking the new subjects (test set) covariates 

Z_shrink_test    <- t(apply(X=azc_test, MARGIN = 1, FUN = function(x){x + z_bar})) #shrunk predictors

X_shrink_test <- cbind(icpt=rep(1,n.test), Z_shrink_test) 

```

Train set model fit on shrunk covariates
```{r}
train_shrunk <- data.frame("WEI" = train_set$weight) 

train_shrunk <- cbind(train_shrunk, Z_shrink) #dataframe with weight observed and shrunk train covariates

mod_OLS_shrunk <- lm(formula = form1, data = train_shrunk) #linear regression with shrunk train covariates

#building dataframe for visualization:
shrinkplot <- rbind(data.frame(relvar = relvar_OLS, 
                               pred = mod_OLS_base$fitted.values, 
                               type = "OLS"), 
                    data.frame(relvar = relvar_it, 
                               pred = mod_OLS_shrunk$fitted.values, 
                               type = "shrunk"))
shrinkplot$pat.id <- c(1:n, 1:n)

Z_compare      <- rbind(Z_ols, Z_shrink) 

Z_compare     <- as.data.frame(Z_compare) 

Z_compare$type <- shrinkplot$type 

Z_compare$pat.id <- c(1:n, 1:n) 
```


Test set- local shrinkage predictions
```{r}
test_shrunk <- data.frame("WEI" = test_set$weight) #observed test reponse weight

test_shrunk <- cbind(test_shrunk, Z_shrink_test) #data frame with weight observed and shrunk covariates

pred_local_test <- predict(mod_OLS_shrunk,newdata= test_shrunk) #predictions

```


Visualization of predictions: OLS and Local shrinkage
 
```{r}
ggplot(
  data = data.frame(pred_ols = pred_ols,
                    pred_local_test = pred_local_test),
  aes(x = pred_ols, y = pred_local_test)
) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, color = "red") +
  labs(
    x = "OLS predictions",
    y = "Local shrinkage predictions"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

Ridge regression, model 1

```{r}
x_train <- model.matrix( ~ HEI + AGE + PUL + SYS, train_set)[,-1] 
y_train <- train_set$WEI
x_test <- model.matrix( ~ HEI + AGE + PUL + SYS, test_set)[,-1] 

ridge_fit <- glmnet(
  x_train,
  y_train,
  alpha = 0, #ridge regression
  lambda = 0.1
)

pred_ridge <- predict(  #ridge test set predictions
  ridge_fit,
  newx = x_test,
  s = 0.1
)
```

Visualization of predictions:  ridge regression and local shrinkage
```{r}
plot(x= pred_ridge, y= pred_local_test, xlab = "Ridge predictions", ylab = "Local shrinkage predictions", main = "Predictions ridge vs local shrinkage")
abline(a = 0, b = 1, col= "red")
```
